title: Managing IT Projects Effectively
overview: This course is designed to equip participants with the essential knowledge and skills needed to effectively manage an Information Technology (IT) project from start to finish. Throughout this interactive program, participants will explore the critical tools and techniques required to lead IT projects successfully. Key topics include requirement analysis, project planning, budget development, team leadership, and performance evaluation.
audience: This course is ideal for project managers and senior IT professionals who are responsible for managing IT projects of varying sizes or who wish to expand their expertise in project management. It is particularly suited to those who want to complement their technical IT knowledge with essential project management skills.
methodology: The course employs a variety of interactive methods, including individual and group exercises that focus on key contract management activities. It also includes case studies and role-playing scenarios, followed by group discussions. The course incorporates pre and post-course assessments to measure learning outcomes.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Manage IT projects using various project management methodologies.
Evaluate the business case for IT projects to ensure feasibility and sound justification.
Align project requirements and objectives with stakeholder needs in a clear and persuasive manner.
Understand and apply fundamental project planning activities and processes, setting realistic and measurable objectives for time and cost using proven planning techniques.
Manage IT projects utilizing agile methodologies and distinguish between traditional and agile project approaches.
Understand the role of the project manager during the design and implementation phases of a project.
Outline key activities during the execution phase and establish effective control processes to ensure alignment with project plans.

items.text: Understanding the unique aspects of IT projects
Waterfall, Incremental, Iterative, and Agile Development Models
Roles and responsibilities of an IT Project Manager
Estimating project duration and resource needs
Developing a network diagram and conducting critical path analysis
Schedule planning using Gantt and Milestone charts
Risk management and disaster recovery planning
Evaluating solution alternatives: build, buy, or outsource
The project manager’s role during the design phase
Addressing challenges during the implementation phase
Managing the project team, schedule, and cost
System testing, change management, and configuration management
